name: Barbados, St Lucia, Grenadines: Soufrière, Kingstown, Bequia

cities.base: The south coast from Hastings to Worthing or Rockley: 5 to 10 minutes to the Garrison, Oistins and the boardwalk, with Bridgetown a short ride away.
cities.name: Barbados

cities.base: Soufrière town or the Malgretoute and Anse Chastanet side, near Sulphur Springs, Diamond Falls and the Gros Piton trail. By air; no direct Barbados flight confirmed.
cities.name: Soufrière, St Lucia

cities.base: Villa and Indian Bay on the Young Island channel, or Kingstown itself for the market and gardens. About 45 minutes' flight from Barbados; airport taxi about $15.
cities.name: Kingstown, St Vincent

cities.base: Port Elizabeth on Admiralty Bay, by the Belmont Walkway. The Bequia Express from Kingstown is EC$25, about an hour, from about 08:00; fewer boats at weekends.
cities.name: Bequia (Port Elizabeth)

places.name: St Nicholas Abbey
places.note: Founded 1658 and one of three genuine Jacobean mansions in the Western Hemisphere, with a rum distillery and a steam railway. A listing shows about 17 with no currency named, so check the price and book on its site. Closed Saturdays.

places.name: George Washington House
places.note: Washington stayed two months here in 1751, his only trip abroad. A 1700s plantation house with tunnels underneath, a short film and an audio guide; $20 adult, $10 for children 5 to 12. Two hours, open daily.

places.name: Barbados Museum & Historical Society
places.note: Seven galleries and 5,000 objects from prehistory to now, in a 19th-century British military prison with a preserved cell and old maps. About $10 on a listing (likely BBD 20), check the price. Closed Sundays and bank holidays.

places.name: Nidhe Israel Synagogue & Museum
places.note: The synagogue dates to 1654 by its own site, one of the oldest in the Americas, inside the UNESCO zone. Listed as free but a reviewer paid a fee, so check the price. Weekdays only, 09:00 to 15:00.

places.name: Garrison Savannah
places.note: Part of UNESCO's Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison (2011): colonial barracks and stone military buildings round a racetrack in use since the 1800s. A listing shows a 9.92 fee with no currency, check the price. The Derby is the first Saturday of March.

places.name: Mount Gay Visitors' Centre
places.note: An 18th-century distillery: a tour of about an hour with a short film and a four-rum tasting, $27.50. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

places.name: Cool Runnings snorkel lunch cruise
places.note: Five hours on a catamaran, 09:30 to 14:30: snorkelling with gear, a buffet lunch, unlimited drinks and hotel transfers, $110 (BBD 220) per adult. Leaves from Hincks Street in Bridgetown.

places.name: St Michael's Cathedral
places.note: A wooden church of 1628 replaced in coral stone, completed 1789, Gothic Revival. Free. Closed Mondays, and Sundays only 07:00 to 12:00 for services.

places.name: National Heroes Square
places.note: The former Trafalgar Square, with Nelson's statue, the cenotaph and the Dolphin fountain beside Parliament. Free, twenty minutes on a Bridgetown walk.

places.name: Parliament Buildings
places.note: Coral stone with a clock tower; a reviewer calls it the third-oldest parliament in the hemisphere, from 1639. Its Museum of Parliament and National Heroes Gallery are temporarily closed, so it is the outside only.

places.name: Exchange Museum
places.note: Currency and economic history, the Freemasons and a Bajan classroom. A 2019 visitor paid BBD 20, about $10; check the price. Closed Sundays, under an hour.

places.name: Cricket Legends of Barbados
places.note: Memorabilia from the 1900s on, Sobers, Haynes and Greenidge, near Kensington Oval. Price not listed, check the price, and call ahead: reviewers report unexpected closures. Saturdays 10:00 to 15:00, closed Sundays.

places.name: Richard Haynes Boardwalk
places.note: 1.6 km of boardwalk on the sea between Accra Beach and Rockley; free and open all hours. Walk it early, or after 16:00 when the heat drops.

places.name: Harry Bayley Observatory
places.note: A 16-inch telescope and Friday evening talks; a small donation is asked. Open Friday and Saturday 19:00 to 22:00. A Sunday listing may be an error, check.

places.name: Champers
places.note: A seafront terrace on the south coast. Bajan fried flying fish is BBD 45 and the catch of the day BBD 62, so about $45 to $55 a head with a starter. Saturdays dinner only, from 17:00; book for dinner.

places.name: Oistins Fish Fry
places.note: Friday night is the event, to about 02:00: fish plates BBD 35 to 45, $18 to $23, as of mid-2026, kingfish or snapper to BBD 55, from stalls like Pat's Place and Uncle George's. Arrive 19:00 to 20:00. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Cocktail Kitchen
places.note: Bajan-modern plates: oxtail with breadfruit coucou BBD 50, roast breadfruit and lobster the signature, cocktails BBD 22 to 32, so $50 to $60 with a drink. Open to midnight; one source has Saturday from 10:00, hours vary, check.

places.name: Cuzz's Cafe Fish Stand
places.note: Flying fish on salt bread with pink pepper sauce from a blue shack by the beach, about $8 to $12 a sandwich. Cash, and a queue at lunch. Saturdays from 09:00 to 16:00; one source says 07:00 to 15:00 daily, hours vary, check.

places.name: Lisa's Doubles & Roti
places.note: Trinidadian doubles and channa with hot pepper sauce; a reviewer paid BBD 12, $6, for a chicken roti. Bring cash. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Nishi
places.note: Japanese-Caribbean dinner in Holetown, about $40 to $60 a person. Closed Tuesdays; one source has it from 18:00, so book and check.

places.name: Cutters of Barbados
places.note: Flying fish cutters and rum punch on the east coast, about $10 to $20 a head. Hours vary, check: one listing shuts at 17:00 on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, another says closed Tuesdays.
places.neighborhood: Bathsheba and Crane side, east coast

places.name: Gros Piton Nature Trail
places.note: The Pitons are UNESCO-listed; Gros Piton is a steep rocky scramble with a mandatory guide, 4 to 6 hours. A reviewer paid EC$125, about $50, at the foreign rate. The gate is open 07:00 to 14:00, so start at 07:00.

places.name: Sulphur Springs
places.note: The drive-in volcano in the Qualibou caldera, mud and warm pools; wear clothes you can ruin. About $15 per a reviewer, not an official price. Go early, before the shuttles.

places.name: Diamond Falls Botanical Gardens & Mineral Baths
places.note: Part of 2,000 acres granted to the Devaux family by Louis XIV in 1713: gardens, the falls and mineral baths. $7 on the page, cash only, and no swimming under the falls. Sundays close at 15:00.

places.name: Tet Paul Nature Trail
places.note: A guided trail with steps and views of both Pitons, St Vincent and Martinique. About $10 on a listing with no currency named, check the price; the sunset visit is about $45. An hour on the trail.

places.name: Morne Coubaril Estate
places.note: A cocoa plantation from the 1740s, Devaux-owned from the mid-1700s, with a replica donkey-powered mill; tours about every half hour. A listing shows 12 with no currency, check the price. The house is private. Sundays to 15:00.

places.name: Pigeon Island National Landmark
places.note: Fort Rodney and 18th-century British and French ruins on 44 acres joined by a causeway, with an Interpretation Centre of colonial and Amerindian finds, usually open weekdays. About $10 cash per reviewers; last entry 16:15.
places.neighborhood: Gros Islet, Rodney Bay, 28 km north

places.name: Anse Chastanet Beach
places.note: Reef snorkelling with turtles off the beach north of town, reached by a rough road. Free; a reviewer paid about $66 for two chairs.

places.name: New Jerusalem Mineral Baths
places.note: A jungle path to warm and cool mineral pools. Hours are erratic, so call ahead, and check the price. Sunday morning is quietest.

places.name: Marie's Local Cuisine
places.note: A flat $20 plate per its listing: chicken or fish with lentils, plantain and pasta, or the buffet. Daytime only, 08:00 to 16:00 every day.

places.name: Botanic Gardens
places.note: Founded 1765, 20 acres, with a breadfruit descended from Bligh's tree and a St Vincent parrot aviary. $5, a guide about $6 (EC$15) an hour. Ninety minutes, in the morning.

places.name: Fort Charlotte
places.note: Begun 1763, finished 1806, about 600 feet above the sea, built for 600 troops and 34 guns and never in action. Free, but guides ask EC$10, about $4. Reviewers in March and May 2026 found renovation work, so access may need permission.

places.name: Dark View Falls
places.note: Two waterfalls, a bamboo bridge and 50 steps to the upper fall; about EC$5, $2. Allow one to two hours' drive each way, so make it a morning.

places.name: Wallilabou Bay film set
places.note: What is left of the Pirates of the Caribbean set on the leeward coast. Fodor's lists a $2 entry with no currency named, so check the price. The Wallilabou Anchorage restaurant is on the bay.

places.name: Kingstown Fish Market
places.note: The town's fish market, busiest on Friday and Saturday mornings. Free to walk round; closed Sundays.

places.name: St Mary's Cathedral
places.note: The Roman Catholic cathedral; sources date it 1820 or 1823, so take the date loosely. Free, open from 06:00 every day, to 21:00 at weekends. Thirty minutes.

places.name: Kingstown Methodist Church
places.note: Established in 1841 by freed slaves per its listing, with late-19th-century pews. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: National Trust (old Carnegie library)
places.note: Carib and Arawak artefacts in the 1909 Carnegie library building. Hours and admission are not listed, so check the price and the hours before you go.

places.name: Driftwood Restaurant & Lounge
places.note: Catch of the day EC$77, conch fritters EC$44 and a ribeye EC$130 on its delivery menu, so a main runs about $18 to $30. Closed Tuesdays per Google; the delivery app lists far shorter hours, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Cafe Soleil
places.note: The Big Bites fish pot is EC$72.72 and the shrimp fiesta EC$86.84 on its delivery menu, about $23 to $32 a main; burgers from EC$28.73. Closed Mondays; weekends close at 21:00, hours vary, check.

places.name: Bungalow (by Flow)
places.note: From the Flow team: a roti EC$27, fish coconut curry EC$50, pizzas EC$30 to 52 and cocktails EC$21 to 25, about $17 to $22 a meal. Weekend lunch from 12:00. Closed Tuesdays per Google, not per the app; hours vary, check.

places.name: Flowt Beach Bar
places.note: Grilled fish EC$23, jerk pork EC$19, steak EC$38, a Hairoun EC$7 and rum punch EC$14, so $11 to $19 a meal. Closed Fridays per the delivery app though Google lists Friday hours; hours vary, check.

places.name: Fort Hamilton
places.note: A late-18th-century battery on a 300-foot hill over Admiralty Bay, a few cannon and the view. Named for Alexander Hamilton, whose father lived on Bequia 1774 to 1790; Alexander never came. Fee not listed, check the price.

places.name: Friendship Bay Beach
places.note: Quieter than Lower Bay and free. The water gets choppy in winter, and visitors have complained about sargassum.

places.name: Jack's Beach Bar
places.note: On Princess Margaret Beach: cocktails EC$18 to 27, wings EC$22 and rosemary fries EC$18 with VAT on its 2024 drinks menu; mains not priced. Tuesday barbecue. Steep stairs, hard at night; hours vary, check.

places.name: Coco's Place
places.note: Open daily 08:00 to 22:00 and to 04:00 on Fridays, the late night on Bequia in this list. Menu prices not found, so check the price.

places.name: De Reef
places.note: At Lower Bay, the long white-sand beach with reef pools, open 10:00 to 21:00. Menu prices not found, so check the price.

places.name: Mac's Pizzeria & Kitchen
places.note: Brick-oven pizza on the Belmont Walkway since 1980, 17 toppings and a lobster pizza. A 2017 bill put a large pizza at EC$34 to 50, about $13 to $19; expect more now. Closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Frangipani Restaurant & Bar
places.note: The hotel restaurant on the waterfront. A 2020 guide put mains at EC$55 to 85, about $20 to $31, and the Thursday barbecue buffet at EC$97 from November to April; expect more now. Happy hour 17:00 to 19:00.

places.name: Dawn's Creole Restaurant
places.note: Conch curry and red snapper at Lower Bay; book for dinner. A 2017 bill for a shared burger, fries, two Cokes and a rum punch was EC$25, about $9; expect more now. Closed Mondays, though a 2020 guide said Wednesdays, check.

places.name: Green Boley Bar
places.note: A roti stop by the Belmont Walkway. A 2017 bill put a roti at EC$6 to 12, $2 to $4; expect more now. Open daily 09:00 to 20:00.

places.name: Rabot Restaurant and The Cacao Bar
places.note: Hotel Chocolat's cocoa estate restaurant, GBP 29 to 45, about $39 to $61, in an undated guide; the Cacao Bar runs 10:00 to 23:00. Lunch 12:00 to 15:00, dinner 18:00 to 22:00.

places.name: Martha's Tables
places.note: Weekday Creole lunch: fish creole, pan-fried chicken, lobster in season, with rice, beans and mac pie. GBP 18 to 27, about $24 to $36, in an undated guide. Booking required; closed weekends. Pair with Sulphur Springs.

places.name: Island Chef
places.note: A Creole plate with drinks for about GBP 15, $20, per an undated guide. Saturdays it closes at 12:00; hours vary, check.

outings.why: The taller Piton by its only trail from Fond Gens Libre, a steep rocky scramble with a mandatory guide, 4 to 6 hours. The gate opens 07:00 and shuts 14:00, so start early.
outings.name: Gros Piton climb
outings.fallback: Tet Paul Nature Trail, an hour with both Pitons in view.

outings.why: St Vincent's volcano, which erupted in April 2021: about 6 km each way from Rabacca, roughly 2 hours up, guide required for foreigners, trail hours 07:30 to 15:30. Rabacca is 1h20 from Kingstown. Confirm the trail is open.
outings.name: La Soufrière volcano, windward trail
outings.fallback: Dark View Falls, two waterfalls in the north.

outings.why: Cool Runnings, 09:30 to 14:30: snorkel stops, buffet lunch, unlimited drinks and hotel transfers, $110 a head.
outings.name: Snorkel lunch catamaran from Bridgetown
outings.fallback: The Richard Haynes Boardwalk and Oistins.

destination.name: Barbados, St Lucia, Grenadines: Soufrière, Kingstown, Bequia
destination.pitch: Four islands in eight to ten days: Barbados for rum, Oistins and the Garrison, Soufrière for the Pitons and a volcano you drive into, then a flight to St Vincent and the ferry to Bequia, where the days shrink to a beach and a roti.
destination.caveat: Hurricane season runs June to November, and Hurricane Beryl in 2024 disrupted the Grenadines ferries into 2025. Every hop is a flight or a timetabled ferry, thinner at weekends, and Barbados is dear: resorts from $450 a night in peak season, 10 to 15 percent service on bills. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Oistins on a Friday night, flying fish cutters at Cuzz's, Champers on the south coast, Marie's $20 Creole plate in Soufrière, Driftwood's catch on St Vincent and Mac's lobster pizza on Bequia.
because.nature: The guided scramble up Gros Piton, Sulphur Springs in the Qualibou caldera, Diamond Falls, Dark View Falls and the La Soufrière volcano trail on St Vincent, and Kingstown's botanic gardens from 1765.
because.culture: Mostly Barbados: the UNESCO Garrison, Nidhe Israel from 1654, George Washington House, St Nicholas Abbey from 1658 and the Barbados Museum. Then Fort Charlotte on St Vincent and Fort Hamilton on Bequia.
because.adventure: Gros Piton with a guide from 07:00, the La Soufrière crater trail from Rabacca, and snorkelling off a Bridgetown catamaran.
because.relaxation: Princess Margaret Beach below Jack's on Bequia, Friendship Bay, the reef off Anse Chastanet, a catamaran lunch out of Bridgetown and the south-coast boardwalk after 16:00.
